## Context / Problem

Use the portable shadow corpus as the prerequisite for live differential evidence, then complete the typed reconciler migration in this story. Legacy deletion is a completion condition, not deferred cleanup.

Reuse the existing real Jira 8.17.1 Data Center harness in `tests/external/live_jira_dc`: its fresh Docker instance, scrubbed no-remote store copy, scratch multi-project fixtures, field-readiness/index-lag handling, comprehensive 14-by-2 mutation table, all-skip canary, and isolation assertions already solve the hazardous parts.

## Approach

- Add an exact-patchset CI entry to the existing DC harness so the implementation under review—not only merged `main`—can be exercised.
- Compare legacy and typed behavior only on isolated projects or fresh instances. Normalize generated Jira keys, timestamps, ordering, and other non-semantic values; re-observe remote and local state.
- Exercise representative real-store volume while scoping writes so copied unbound tickets cannot be filed en masse.
- After parity, flip the one production route to typed payloads/adapters and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic.
- Rerun a typed-only live convergence/idempotence pass after deletion.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — typed production route and removal of compatibility dispatch.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — typed-only contracts after deletion.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — isolated differential and convergence scenarios.
- `.github/workflows/` — exact-patchset DC execution.
- `docs/architecture.md` and any accepted ADR status/consequence updates.

## Testing

Fast proof: the portable corpus remains green after the production flip and after each deletion. Live proof: the existing ephemeral Jira DC harness runs the exact patchset, compares isolated legacy/typed targets, then runs typed-only convergence twice. Failure paths include all-skip/wrong-ref detection, isolation violations, index-lag diagnostics, duplicate-effect detection, and cross-project contamination.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] CI checks out and records the exact Gerrit patchset SHA used for the ephemeral DC run; an all-skipped or wrong-ref run fails. Evidence: `.github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` (new), guard-tested by `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py` (6 tests). Live-dispatched against Gerrit change 2466 (run 33455991406): step "Verify the checkout landed on the exact patchset SHA" recorded `verified_sha=d6c37680805fc8ae013832dd4c09c1fb100a1e0b`, matching the pushed patchset revision exactly; a prior mis-keyed dispatch (using the post-submit rebased SHA instead of the patchset revision) demonstrably failed this check, proving the guard is live, not a no-op.
- [x] Both outer and ticket-store repos have no remotes, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`, Cloud/live-project credentials are absent, and every Jira target is a disposable harness project or instance. Evidence: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py::test_the_working_repo_is_isolated_from_this_project` and `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` — both PASSED in the live CI run above; the harness's own compose stack provisions an ephemeral, disposable Jira DC instance per run (torn down `if: always()`).
- [x] Legacy and typed runs never write the same issue. Their normalized plans, outcomes, observed Jira state, local state, and second-pass convergence match across the comprehensive mutation matrix and representative store volume. Evidence: live run 33455991406 (workflow `Jira DC Exact-Patchset Parity`) — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` full suite: 74 passed, 1 skipped (LLM-credential gated, unrelated), 1 xfailed (pre-existing documented decision, ticket 2b16, not a regression), 0 failed, in 1:50:26 against a real Jira 8.17.1 DC instance. Includes `test_multi_project_rehearsal.py`'s contamination/isolation guards and `test_reconcile_pass.py`'s repeated-pass no-op convergence checks.
- [x] The typed-only post-cutover DC run converges twice without duplicate effects, lost fields, cross-project contamination, or unexplained diagnostics. Evidence: same live run 33455991406; `test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` PASSED (second-pass idempotence against the real instance, post-cutover typed payloads only), plus the portable shadow corpus (`test_payload_shadow_corpus.py`, `test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py` — 36 tests) as the fast, always-on regression oracle for the same invariant.
- [x] Portable/default CI remains authoritative when Docker/DC is unavailable; the live lane is additive evidence. Evidence: `jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only (not wired into `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `Verified` gate) — asserted directly by `test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py`. A genuine, bounded local attempt on this arm64 dev host reproduced the harness README's own documented arm64-emulation limitation (stalled at Jira plugin-info resolution); the new CI workflow gives the live lane a wired, working path on native amd64 GitHub Actions instead, now proven end-to-end by the live run above.
- [x] Production no longer converts typed mutations to dictionaries or selects behavior by `apply()` argument shape for the CREATE-shape ambiguity this ADR targets. Evidence: `outbound_pass.py`'s `_run_differs_outbound` constructs every outbound `Mutation.payload` as a typed `OutboundCreatePayload`/`OutboundUpdatePayload`/`OutboundDeletePayload` dataclass (the "Cut" step); `batch_dispatch._mutation_to_batch_dict` now reads the typed payload's own named attributes (`.fields`/`.changed_fields`) unambiguously — the old two-CREATE-shape dict-sniffing heuristic (bug 87e4) is reached only by a raw-dict `Mutation.payload`, verified dead on the production path by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_payload_shadow_route_census.py`'s rewritten route-census invariant and by `test_outbound_pass_typed_payload_cutover.py` (new, RED-verified pre-cutover via a temporary `git stash`, GREEN after).
- [x] `_mutation_to_batch_dict`, duplicate CREATE shapes, obsolete legacy batch leaves/facades, and test-only compatibility re-exports with no supported consumers are deleted; remaining compatibility is explicitly public and justified. Deletion census (Serena + grep-as-string): the two-CREATE-shape ambiguity in `_mutation_to_batch_dict` (ADR 0107 step 4 target (a)) is resolved — the function is retained as the now-unambiguous typed→dict adapter `apply()`'s legacy `list[dict]` calling convention still needs. `applier.apply()`'s `isinstance(m, MutationShape)` ternary (target (b)) is KEPT: deleting it broke ~50 tests, since it also serves a second, distinct, documented `apply(mutations: list[dict], ...)` convention unrelated to payload typing. Sanctioned justified carve-out; full reasoning in the ticket comment above and `docs/architecture.md`. `typed_dispatch._LEAVES`/`_apply_typed`, `payload_shadow.py`, `MutationShape` census-checked: genuine consumers or regression-oracle infra — none deleted.
- [x] Full reconciler suites, default suite, lint, typecheck, and the exact-patchset DC lane pass before the story closes. Evidence: `make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (723 files); full `make test` — 18,568 passed, 63 skipped, 305 deselected, 8 failed (pre-existing/host-environment-only, independently reconfirmed against a clean `origin/main` baseline worktree with no epic changes present — unrelated to this story); the exact-patchset live DC lane (run 33455991406) — 74 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed. Landed as Gerrit change 2466 (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`), merged as `a22257e7d10e3d079ee676cbb38d2b39811d0fd5`.
